question: How does true consciousness differ from the measuring activity of the limited knower?
premises: Dependent knowing is mere measuring constructed by a limited knower.
Consciousness may surge forth in manifestation.
Consciousness is free from temporal sequence.
inference: Unlike constructed measuring, consciousness manifests without being divided by temporal sequence.
uncertainties: prācyapramātṛ may refer to a prior or ordinary limited subject; the gloss keeps it general.
plain_english: That dependent knowing is only a kind of measuring, constructed by the limited knower. Consciousness, even when it surges forth, is not divided by temporal sequence.
